message.content:
The title “best jazz singer” is highly subjective and depends on what you value—vocal technique, emotional depth, influence, or innovation. Below is a list of some of the most celebrated jazz vocalists, each known for a distinct style and lasting impact on the genre. (No single singer can claim an absolute “best” spot, but these names are frequently cited as the most influential and revered.)

| Singer | Era | Signature Style / Contributions |
|--------|-----|---------------------------------|
| **Billie Holiday** | 1930s‑1960s | Pioneered a deeply personal, emotionally raw delivery; her phrasing and timing set a new standard for jazz vocalists. |
| **Ella Fitzgerald** | 1940s‑1990s | Known as the “First Lady of Song,” her impeccable diction, scat‑singing mastery, and pure tone made her a benchmark for vocal excellence. |
| **Sarah Vaughan** | 1940s‑2000s | Her rich, operatic voice and wide range earned her the nickname “Sassy.” She blended jazz with blues and pop sensibilities. |
| **Nat King Cole** | 1940s‑1965 | A smooth baritone who bridged jazz and popular music; his phrasing and relaxed swing made him a crossover icon. |
| **Cassandra Wilson** | 1980s‑present | Blends jazz with folk, blues, and world music; her husky tone and innovative arrangements keep her at the forefront of contemporary jazz. |
| **Diana Krall** | 1990s‑present | Combines jazz standards with a modern pop sensibility; her piano‑vocal duo format has earned her worldwide acclaim. |
| **Nina Simone** | 1950s‑2003 | Though often labeled “soul” or “R&B,” her jazz roots and powerful, politically charged performances make her a pivotal figure. |
| **Tony Bennett** | 1950s‑present | A master of the Great American Songbook, his warm baritone and impeccable phrasing have earned him enduring respect. |
| **Al Jarreau** | 1970s‑2018 | Known for his smooth, soulful voice and ability to blend jazz with R&B and pop; his scat and vocal improvisation were groundbreaking. |
| **Esperanza Spalding** | 2000s‑present | A bassist‑vocalist who fuses jazz with funk, soul, and world music; her technical skill and compositional prowess set her apart. |

### How to Choose Your “Best”
- **If you value technical mastery and vocal range:** Ella Fitzgerald or Sarah Vaughan.
- **If you prefer emotional depth and storytelling:** Billie Holiday or Nina Simone.
- **If you like a blend of jazz with other genres:** Cassandra Wilson or Esperanza Spalding.
- **If you enjoy a smooth, crossover appeal:** Diana Krall or Tony Bennett.

Feel free to explore recordings from each artist to see which style resonates most with you!
